reader_notes: Short single-question unit. The Hallvik example is constructed so that all three competing explanations are removed at once (no windows, white liner), which makes the function-of-the-example question clean and single-answered.

The underlying physics is right (water absorbs long wavelengths more strongly, effect scales with path length), and the white-liner point is consistent with it rather than tacked on: reflection doubles the path, it does not add pigment.
